findings: Scoped batch workers join before return; only the coordinator writes status.
Final status report precedes durable local checkpoint commit; failure retains exact intent and old checkpoint.
Partial remote HEAD success remains recoverable through the existing intent and retry order.
Activation changes only the publisher executable and retains source, arguments, publisher identity, namespace and seven protected processes.
Activation requires checkpoint progress after a floor captured under the same verified new process; old-process progress is insufficient.
Approved patch, donor, all 963 source records, 34 dependency graph records, eight regression names and release hashes are pinned.
Rollback checks source, registry, protected processes and owned old/new unit bytes before restoration.
limits: Status reporting adds no total batch deadline.
Existing 300-second cloud progress and 8192-event backlog gates remain unchanged.
An entered remote request can complete after a status error; cancellation prevents later stages where possible and all scoped workers join.
Activation cloud proof fully reads catalog HEAD and the last commit metadata; it does not read the payload frame.
